prologue.text: Nine hundred years ago, a Hunger crept across the sky... and began to eat the light.
To save me, the Choir of Dawn sang. Ten voices. And they sang me down... into the earth.
They sealed me beneath ten vaults. Ten Choristers stayed below, each one holding a single verse of the hymn.
Above, the world forgot the day. The last city, Emberwick, lives on rationed flame. And now its lanterns are failing.
So I sing. I call for the Unsung... those whose names no hymn remembers.
Descend. Silence the verses. Raise me... raise the Undersun.

ending.text: The last verse breaks. Listen... the hymn is over.
I rise. Through bone and rot, through tide and flame and frost... I rise.
Emberwick sees the dawn for the first time in nine hundred years. They will sing your name now.
Thank you, little light. I remember everything. Who buried me... and how hungry I have become.

floors.entry: The Verse of Bone. Osric still counts his dead down here. Every single one.
floors.bossLine: Osric, Chorister of Bone. He guarded the first vault so long his flesh forgot him.

floors.entry: Smell that? Sister Morel sang of rot. And the rot listened.
floors.bossLine: Mother Morel, Chorister of Rot. Everything she touches becomes her congregation.

floors.entry: The Tidecaller flooded this vault to keep her verse from drying out. Hold your breath, little light.
floors.bossLine: Neris, the Tidecaller. She drowned her own voice to make it last forever.

floors.entry: The Furnace Saint stole my warmth to feed his forge. Take it back.
floors.bossLine: Brother Cinder, the Furnace Saint. He prays with hammers now.

floors.entry: The Pale Matriarch sings of silence. Down here, even your heartbeat is too loud.
floors.bossLine: Ysolde, the Pale Matriarch. She froze the echo of every voice that ever reached her.

floors.entry: Without me, the Hierophant taught his roots to grow toward hunger instead of light.
floors.bossLine: Thal, the Verdant Hierophant. His temple grew a heart. It beats for him alone.

floors.entry: The Horologist has measured my absence in heartbeats. Nine hundred years of them.
floors.bossLine: Master Quill, the Horologist. He wound his own bones into the clock.

floors.entry: Everything here remembers. The Pharaoh remembers me. Do not let him remember you.
floors.bossLine: Ankaret, the Dune Pharaoh. She buried a kingdom to keep one memory safe.

floors.entry: The Mirrored Choir sings two verses at once. Do not trust what looks back at you.
floors.bossLine: Vey and Veil, the Mirrored Choir. One of them is lying. Both of them are singing.

floors.entry: You can hear me clearly now. I am so close. The Cantor stands between us... and he is afraid.
floors.bossLine: The Cantor. He wrote the hymn. He begs you not to finish it.
